## CodeQL / Cache Poisoning via execution of untrusted code

Potential cache poisoning in the context of the default branch due to privilege checkout of untrusted code from [matrix.ref](1). ([workflow_dispatch](2)).

[Show more details](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/security/code-scanning/779)

+name: Agent startup benchmark
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      baseline:
+        description: Baseline same-repository branch or full commit SHA
+        required: true
+        default: main
+        type: string
+      candidate:
+        description: Candidate same-repository branch or full commit SHA
+        required: true
+        default: main
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: agent-startup-benchmark
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  prepare:
+    if: github.repository == 'open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    outputs:
+      baseline: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.baseline }}
+      candidate: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.candidate }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Resolve revisions on repository branches
+        id: resolve
+        env:
+          BASELINE: ${{ inputs.baseline }}
+          CANDIDATE: ${{ inputs.candidate }}
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          for variant in baseline candidate; do
+            if [[ "$variant" == baseline ]]; then ref="$BASELINE"; else ref="$CANDIDATE"; fi
+            if [[ "$ref" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
+              sha=$(git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options "$ref^{commit}")
+            else
+              git check-ref-format "refs/heads/$ref"
+              sha=$(git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options "refs/remotes/origin/$ref^{commit}")
+            fi
+            # Exclude pull refs and commits reachable only through a fork.
+            branches=$(git for-each-ref --contains="$sha" --format='%(refname)' refs/remotes/origin/)
+            test -n "$branches"
+            printf '%s=%s\n' "$variant" "$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          done
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version-file: .java-version
+
+      - name: Validate and package common standalone benchmark
+        working-directory: benchmark-overhead
+        run: ./gradlew test --tests 'io.opentelemetry.startup.*Test' startupRecorderJar
+
+      - name: Package trusted harness, not candidate sources
+        run: |
+          git rev-parse HEAD > harness-revision.txt
+          tar --exclude=benchmark-overhead/build --exclude=benchmark-overhead/.gradle \
+            -czf startup-harness.tar.gz benchmark-overhead .java-version buildscripts/spotless.license.java harness-revision.txt
+
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: startup-harness
+          path: startup-harness.tar.gz
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 30
+
+  build:
+    needs: prepare
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 45
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - variant: baseline
+            ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.baseline }}
+          - variant: candidate
+            ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.candidate }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ matrix.ref }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version-file: .java-version
+
+      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@3f5f9adaf7d9fecd50b5935e54106014257a94e6 # v6.4.0
+        with:
+          cache-read-only: true
+
+      - name: Build exact agent
+        run: ./gradlew :javaagent:shadowJar -PremoveJarVersionNumbers=true "-Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1g" --max-workers=2
+
+      - name: Record source and artifact identity

The volume has no session-scoped cleanup registration, and the workflow cleanup only deletes `$AGENTS`. Register the volume with the Testcontainers reaper or add attempt-scoped workflow cleanup that removes only this attempt's Docker resources.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly to fix interrupted-run cleanup identified in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20963#discussion_r4373128627.

AgentStartupBenchmark creates an unlabelled named Docker volume through docker.createVolumeCmd(), then removes it only in a finally block. Cancelling or timing out the workflow can terminate the test JVM before that block runs. The final workflow step only removes $AGENTS, so the volume and copied JARs/recordings can remain on the persistent shared bare-metal host. Testcontainers 2.0.5 ResourceReaper has session/default-label filters, but this raw Docker volume creation is not registered or labelled for those filters.

Make this benchmark's named volume eligible for session-scoped Testcontainers reaper cleanup, or use another narrowly attempt-scoped cleanup mechanism that also works when the test JVM is interrupted. Keep the existing prompt normal-path cleanup, and ensure only resources owned by this benchmark invocation are removed. Do not add broad Docker prune commands, clean unrelated resources, change host settings, or alter AOT benchmark behavior. Reuse the actual supported Testcontainers 2.0.5 APIs and labels rather than inventing a register-volume API. Keep the paired comparison, raw observations, original retained results, and measurement/profile separation unchanged.

Add focused coverage or a reproducible check of the cleanup ownership/registration and, where Docker is available, abrupt-process-exit cleanup. Apply the standalone benchmark's narrow Spotless task before its focused startup tests, and report actual outcomes or environment blockers. Limit changes to this cleanup defect and directly related tests/documentation. Do not modify PR title or description, create another PR, or post replies to human reviewers.

+## Ordinary agent startup comparison
+
+The opt-in `agentStartupBenchmark` task compares ordinary `-javaagent` launches
+of the small Spring smoke application with a baseline and a candidate agent JAR.
+It reuses the pinned JDK 25 image and timing parser from the AOT benchmark,
+without AOT or bootstrap-classpath preloading. Instrumentation and the SDK remain
+active; all exporters are `none`.
+
+Use JDK 25 and Docker with Linux containers. Each application container uses CPUs
+`0,1`, a two-CPU quota, a 1 GiB memory limit, and `-Xmx512m`. The Docker host must
+expose those CPUs as distinct physical cores on the same NUMA node; the workflow
+verifies this before measurement. Do not build artifacts or run other benchmarks
+during measurement.
+
+Build both agents from their respective source revisions with
+`:javaagent:shadowJar`, then run the standalone benchmark:
+
+```sh
+cd benchmark-overhead
+./gradlew agentStartupBenchmark \
+  -PstartupBenchmarkBaseline=/absolute/path/to/baseline.jar \
+  -PstartupBenchmarkCandidate=/absolute/path/to/candidate.jar
+```
+
+The benchmark first runs an A/A control using the same baseline JAR under both
+labels, then compares the baseline and candidate. Each round starts the pair in
+alternating order; comparison rounds also start an uninstrumented application.
+Defaults are two discarded fresh-process starts and twenty measured starts per
+variant and phase. Set
+`-PstartupBenchmarkWarmups=0 -PstartupBenchmarkSamples=2` for a short functional
+run, not a performance conclusion.
+
+The primary metric is JVM uptime at Spring startup completion, including
+`premain()`. HTTP readiness time includes Docker and harness overhead and is
+secondary. Every start must return HTTP 200 and `Hi!` from `/greeting`. Failures
+abort the benchmark and retain diagnostics; samples are not retried or filtered
+as outliers.
+
+Results under `build/reports/agent-startup/<run-id>/` include raw observations,
+host load averages, agent hashes and versions, exact JVM commands, image/JDK
+identity, medians, interquartile ranges, and paired baseline-minus-candidate
+savings. The reported 95% interval uses a circular moving-block bootstrap over
+consecutive rounds. Read it alongside the A/A control and reproduce improvements
+in an independent run.
+
+Separate untimed baseline and candidate launches record startup JFR files and
+execution-sample summaries. A diagnostic-only recorder agent starts JFR before
+OpenTelemetry's `premain()`; the JVM's `-XX:StartFlightRecording` option starts
+too late to capture agent initialization. Those launches are excluded from timing
+results. These are fresh JVMs with warm image/filesystem caches, not cold-machine
+starts or throughput measurements.
+
+Manually dispatch `agent-startup-benchmark.yml` from `main` with `baseline` and
+`candidate` set to same-repository branch names or full commit SHAs. For example,
+use `baseline=main` and `candidate=my-startup-change`. Both revisions must be
+reachable from repository branches, not fork-only commits or pull refs. Dispatch
+requires repository write access; only run trusted code, since agent JARs execute
+on a shared host.
+
+The workflow resolves immutable source identities and builds agents on standard
+hosted runners. A common harness from the workflow revision is packaged
+separately from both agents and unpacked under `RUNNER_TEMP`, without checking
+out sources on the bare-metal host. It measures serially on
+`oracle-bare-metal-64cpu-1024gb-x86-64-ubuntu-24` without repository credentials,
+and uploads source identities, host information, complete reports, and profiles
+as workflow artifacts. Cleanup is limited to the attempt's files and the
+harness's own containers and named volume; it does not prune Docker or tune the
+shared host. This is opt-in tooling, not required PR CI, a scheduled benchmark,
+or a performance threshold gate.
+
+Rerun only the `benchmark` job to repeat measurements with the same built JARs.
+Each attempt uploads a separate `agent-startup-results-<attempt>` artifact,
+retaining the earlier observations.
+
+### Retained startup evidence

@copilot Update this existing PR directly. The user explicitly requested: "do 1-3 + only want that 1 metric". The agreed changes are the three reductions below and JVM start to successful HTTP readiness as the sole startup timing metric.

1. Consolidate workflow inputs into one artifact and one source-revision identity. The agent and benchmark always come from the same selected branch/tag, so remove the separate startup-agent/startup-harness artifact machinery and duplicate revision bookkeeping. Keep the agent checksum, useful reproducibility metadata, per-attempt result artifacts, and the ability to rerun only measurement using the same built inputs.

2. Run focused unit/functional validation only in the hosted build job. Remove the duplicate startup unit-test invocation from the bare-metal measurement job. Preserve necessary benchmark task prerequisites and input checksum verification; this does not authorize dropping validation entirely.

3. Remove the ordinary benchmark's shared named Docker volume. Copy the agent and recorder directly into each application container, and copy the resulting JFR file back out. Remove the ordinary benchmark's preparation container and obsolete volume creator, child-process fixture, cleanup regression test, and its enable flag if no longer used. Preserve Testcontainers-owned container cleanup and narrowly scoped per-attempt filesystem cleanup. Existing AOT benchmark volume usage and behavior must remain unchanged. Avoid replacing the deleted machinery with another general-purpose framework.

The one timing metric must be elapsed JVM lifetime from JVM startup, including the OpenTelemetry premain, to the first successful HTTP readiness response from /greeting with status 200 and body Hi!. The current Spring startup log's process-uptime value ends too early, while the host timer around application.start() begins before Docker setup; neither is the requested metric. Use a reliable JVM-relative observation tied to the successful HTTP response, preferably reported by the application, and document its precise semantics. Do not gate readiness probing on the Spring startup log, silently fall back to that log, subtract unsynchronized clocks, or include container creation/JAR copying in the duration. Retain readiness polling as needed, but do not retry application launches or discard failed samples. Report only this duration in raw timing observations and summary distributions; remove the separate Spring-startup and Docker-inclusive HTTP-duration metrics. Keep raw observations, warmup exclusion, failure diagnostics, resource limits, and the single-sample functional mode.

The existing smoke application image is pinned and immutable. If accurate timing needs a minimal application-fixture change, wire the actually executed fixture into this benchmark and the consolidated inputs; changing a source file while continuing to run the unchanged published image is insufficient. Prefer shipping needed fixture changes with the benchmark inputs rather than requiring image publication. Keep the solution small and targeted. Retain the separate untimed JFR recording and its existing diagnostic summary; dropping JFR diagnostics was option 4 and was not requested. Do not turn the recorder into a timing-run profiling agent.

Update directly related tests, Gradle/workflow wiring, and README to match the one metric and volume-free behavior. Apply the narrow relevant formatting tasks before focused validation; use the repository's mise/rumdl configuration for changed Markdown. Exercise the real Docker-backed startup path where feasible and report exact outcomes or environment blockers. Preserve single-revision dispatch, active instrumentation/SDK with exporters disabled, existing AOT comparisons, and the PR's current base/draft state. Do not restore baseline/candidate comparisons, create a new PR, or post replies to human reviewers.

[General] This synchronous Docker inspection delays the first `/greeting` request after the JVM starts. Because the handler samples current JVM uptime, Docker-daemon latency can inflate the startup measurements even when the application is already ready. Capture the readiness response and profile cutoff immediately after `application.start()`, then collect image metadata.

Readiness is now requested immediately after `application.start()`, and the profile cutoff is captured immediately after the successful response. Docker image inspection and metadata persistence happen afterward, so they no longer delay either observation.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly to fix the actionable timing finding in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20963#discussion_r4374148246.

AgentStartupBenchmark.sample currently starts the application, synchronously inspects the Docker image and fills metadata, and only then calls awaitReadiness. Because /greeting returns the JVM's current uptime, that unrelated Docker-daemon call delays the first readiness request and can inflate the sole startup metric. The JFR cutoff is also captured after metadata persistence.

Immediately after application.start(), capture the successful readiness response and its profile cutoff, before Docker image inspection or metadata persistence. Collect and save image/JDK metadata afterward. Preserve the application's JVM-relative response timestamp, HTTP 200/Hi! validation, failure propagation, and separate untimed JFR diagnostics. Do not replace the metric with Spring log timing or Docker-inclusive host timing.

Keep the fix small: preserve one consolidated input artifact/source identity, hosted-only unit validation, no ordinary shared Docker volume, per-attempt artifacts and cleanup, single-revision dispatch, and existing AOT behavior. Do not introduce new configuration or a general framework for this ordering fix. Apply the narrow relevant formatter, run focused startup tests and the smallest real Docker-backed functional run where feasible, and report genuine validation results or blockers. Do not create another PR or reply to human review threads.

+      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@3f5f9adaf7d9fecd50b5935e54106014257a94e6 # v6.4.0
+        with:
+          cache-read-only: true
+
+      - name: Build agent from selected revision
+        run: ./gradlew :javaagent:shadowJar :smoke-tests:images:spring-boot:classes -PremoveJarVersionNumbers=true "-Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1g" --max-workers=2
+
+      - name: Format and validate standalone benchmark
+        working-directory: benchmark-overhead
+        run: ./gradlew spotlessApply test --tests 'io.opentelemetry.startup.*Test' startupRecorderJar
+
+      - name: Package all benchmark inputs
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/fixture"
+          cp javaagent/build/libs/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/"
+          cp smoke-tests/images/spring-boot/build/classes/java/main/io/opentelemetry/smoketest/springboot/controller/WebController.class \
+            "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/fixture/"
+          cp benchmark-overhead/build/libs/startup-recorder.jar "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/"
+          git rev-parse HEAD > "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/revision.txt"
+          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark" && sha256sum opentelemetry-javaagent.jar startup-recorder.jar > sha256.txt)
+          git archive --format=tar HEAD \
+            benchmark-overhead .java-version buildscripts/spotless.license.java \
+            | gzip -n > "$RUNNER_TEMP/startup-benchmark/harness.tar.gz"
+
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: startup-benchmark
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/startup-benchmark
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          retention-days: 30
+
+  benchmark:
+    needs: build
+    permissions: {}
+    runs-on: oracle-bare-metal-64cpu-1024gb-x86-64-ubuntu-24
+    timeout-minutes: 45
+    steps:
+      - name: Isolate this attempt under runner temporary storage
+        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
+        run: |
+          root="$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-startup-$GITHUB_RUN_ID-$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT"
+          printf 'AGENTS=%s\nGRADLE_USER_HOME=%s/gradle-home\n' "$root" "$root" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
+        with:
+          name: startup-benchmark
+          path: ${{ env.AGENTS }}
+
+      - name: Unpack standalone benchmark
+        run: tar -xzf "$AGENTS/harness.tar.gz" -C "$AGENTS"
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          distribution: temurin
+          java-version-file: ${{ env.AGENTS }}/.java-version
+
+      - name: Verify benchmark input checksums
